note: One case per Rust test of effect/navigate.rs dynamic_prefix_tests (a_slash_terminated_dynamic_prefix_needs_a_page_beneath_it, control_a_declared_detail_page_beneath_the_prefix_satisfies_it, control_a_prefix_without_a_trailing_slash_keeps_prefix_matching, a_dynamic_query_string_resolves_its_route_before_the_question_mark, the_host_sign_in_route_is_reachable_without_a_page, control_an_undeclared_route_is_still_unreachable, control_a_declared_sign_in_page_is_reachable_as_any_page, control_a_static_target_still_matches_its_page), effect/utils.rs (test_navigate_missing_required_payload, test_navigate_with_required_payload; test_path_matches_pattern is covered by the param-segment matching of the pages), and orbital-compiler/tests/expects_page_slice.rs (slice_without_the_declaration_reports_the_navigate_unreachable, expects_page_makes_the_sibling_route_reachable, an_unrelated_expected_route_does_not_satisfy_the_navigate, a_real_declaration_still_wins_over_an_expectation_of_the_same_path), plus the invalid-path, arity, external URL, wholly-dynamic target, lazy page and send-server branches of validate_navigate and validate_send_server. Where several declared pages could match a target the Rust check picks one by hash-map order; the lint picks the first in declaration order (exact path, then param match, then prefix), which agrees whenever one page matches.
